review_type: Independent adversarial review of transport corrections and exact-clone parity blockers
verdict: REJECTED for exact parity. The transport changes are a real improvement and four focused tests independently pass. WSS now attempts TLS, upgrade verification and incremental framing are delegated to a protocol library, and unsupported BLE/WinUSB selections no longer pretend to contact devices. These corrections do not implement the missing device backends, reproduce every reference WebSocket behavior, or close the larger UI and platform gaps.

scores.scale: Provisional qualitative judgment on a 0-10 exact-reference-parity scale. Scores are not completion percentages. They remain coarse because no exhaustive feature inventory or rendered UI certification exists. This incremental repair is too narrow to justify raising a whole-product rating.

independent_validation.scope: Local Windows mp-core tests with loopback TCP peers. The TLS test observes a TLS record prefix then deliberately closes the server. It is not a completed authenticated WSS session or certificate-validation corpus. The fragmentation test splits one frame across TCP writes and read timeouts; it is not a WebSocket continuation-frame test.

confirmed_corrections.status: false-success behavior fixed; feature remains missing
confirmed_corrections.evidence: comms::open now returns ErrorKind::Unsupported for nonempty BLE/WinUSB specs and InvalidInput for blank identifiers. DriverTransport memory queues were removed. Independent test checks unsupported results.
confirmed_corrections.remaining: Actual discovery, permissions, device IO, connection lifecycle and real MAVLink readback are unimplemented. An honest error is not a parity implementation.

confirmed_corrections.prior_finding: R30-02 plaintext WSS, unauthenticated upgrade and partial-read corruption
confirmed_corrections.status: identified implementation defects corrected in inspected paths
confirmed_corrections.evidence: WebSocketTransport uses tungstenite::client_tls with rustls webpki roots; ring provider is initialized when no process provider exists. Client request and frame handling come from tungstenite. Independent tests reject an invalid Sec-WebSocket-Accept, observe TLS rather than HTTP on a wss endpoint and deliver a binary frame after a delayed partial TCP write.
confirmed_corrections.remaining: No completed trusted WSS endpoint test, wrong-host/untrusted/expired-certificate test, WebSocket continuation-frame, ping/pong, close, reconnect, write-backpressure or non-Windows execution was performed in this review.

findings.subsystem: Reference WebSocket application protocol and lifecycle
evidence: Reference RunReader handles text session IDs, responds to text starting with 3 by sending 40/MAVControl, and 5, and logs other text rather than treating it as binary MAVLink.
Reference Write handles its socketio state and RunReader attempts reconnect while autoReconnect is enabled.

Rust WebSocketTransport feeds Message::Text bytes into its MAVLink byte stream, sends only binary frames and returns connection-aborted on close. It contains no Socket.IO negotiation or reconnect state.
findings.impact: A raw binary WS endpoint can work while reference-compatible Socket.IO endpoints and reconnect workflows still differ. Text control traffic is passed to the MAVLink parser.
findings.required_fix: Specify and port the reference endpoint modes, text-control handling, binary envelope and reconnection/cancellation behavior. Do not equate a passing raw loopback with all Mission Planner WebSocket support.
findings.acceptance: Protocol fixture tests for raw WS, reference Socket.IO control exchange and binary envelope, server disconnect/reconnect and explicit user disconnect; actual WS/WSS session with decoded MAVLink telemetry.

evidence: The WSS test checks only the initial TLS record and expected connection failure after peer close.
The new framing tests do not send WebSocket continuation frames, ping/pong or a close handshake.
The code uses a trust-verifying library configuration, which is appropriate, but no actual successful certificate-validated session was exercised by this reviewer.
findings.required_fix: Add a trusted local TLS fixture or an appropriate controlled endpoint, reject wrong-name/untrusted certificates, and verify continuation/control/close behavior and bounded write failures.
findings.acceptance: Authenticated successful WSS telemetry exchange plus deterministic negative certificate tests and meaningful frame/control regression coverage.

evidence: link Shared.inspector is keyed by system/component/message ID and keeps only the last message for that key.
tool_windows::prox_ui reads DISTANCE_SENSOR from this cache, maps every orientation to enum*45 degrees and has no OBSTACLE_DISTANCE path.
findings.required_fix: Retain per-vehicle sensor/sector state separately from the message inspector, validate horizontal orientations and distance sentinels, handle obstacle arrays and expire stale readings.
findings.acceptance: At least eight sectors from one component remain visible together; tests cover vehicle isolation, orientations, sentinels and expiry; rendered reference comparison.

evidence: iOS workflow still compiles a library without an installable Xcode app wrapper.
Mobile serial remains unsupported and important file workflows remain incomplete.
Graph zoom/pan/cursor/expression behavior remains short of the reference and the log UI is not usable at narrow phone widths.
Native diagnostic checks remain partial heuristics with no equivalence corpus against the reference external analyzer.
BLE/WinUSB and missing DFU/STK500 flashing workflows remain implementation gaps.
No complete source-pinned feature inventory or current rendered equivalence matrix exists.
findings.required_fix: Continue against the explicit blockers and create a durable feature/workflow-to-evidence inventory. Validate actual installed apps and device protocols on each required platform.
findings.acceptance: The ten-out-of-ten gates from round-30 remain unsatisfied; no product-wide exact-clone claim is supported.

next_run_priority: Repair the deterministic proximity data-loss and orientation defects with a dedicated per-vehicle model and multi-sector regression tests.
Establish a reference-to-Rust workflow inventory so future ratings are tied to evidence rather than selected examples.
Finish WebSocket endpoint/lifecycle parity and authenticated TLS/control-frame tests.
Implement real BLE/WinUSB backends and installable iOS/mobile document workflows.
Close graph interaction and exact analyzer behavior gaps with reference fixtures and rendered comparisons.
ten_out_of_ten_status: NOT MET. Missing required features, unverified real platform/device paths and lack of comprehensive UI equivalence evidence prevent 10/10 irrespective of passing focused tests.
limitations: Reviewer independently ran only the four focused comms tests, not the full workspace suite.
No UI renders, live vehicles, firmware boards, mobile devices, external network endpoints or platform builds were tested.
This is an adversarial sampled review, not an exhaustive certification of the full reference codebase.
The worktree is mutable; the report describes the transport implementation inspected during this review.
